title: Python Boolean Expressions
description: Combine comparisons with and, or, and not. Read each expression slowly and track the resulting True or False value.

questions.prompt: What must be true for A and B to be True?
questions.explanation: and requires every part of the expression to be true.

questions.code:
age = 14
has_ticket = True
print(age >= 13 and has_ticket)
questions.explanation: Both age >= 13 and has_ticket are true, so and produces True.

questions.prompt: A or expression is True when at least one of its parts is True.
questions.explanation: or needs one or more true parts; it is false only when every part is false.

questions.prompt: What does not True evaluate to?
questions.explanation: not reverses a Boolean value: it changes True to False and False to True.

questions.code:
left = False
right = True
print(left or right)
questions.explanation: The right side is true, so the or expression is true even though the left side is false.

questions.prompt: Which expression means a value is not equal to 10?
questions.explanation: Python writes the not-equal comparison as !=, with an exclamation mark followed by an equals sign.

questions.code:
ready = True
late = False
print(not late and ready)
questions.explanation: not late is True, and ready is also True, so the complete and expression is True.

questions.prompt: An empty string is treated as false in a condition.
questions.explanation: Python considers empty strings, lists, and dictionaries falsy; non-empty ones are truthy.

questions.prompt: In `True or False and False`, which part is grouped first?
options: The whole expression is evaluated left to right
questions.explanation: and has higher precedence than or, so Python evaluates False and False first. Use parentheses when you want the grouping to be obvious to a reader.
7 is greater than 5 and less than 10, so both comparisons are true.
